title: The Lamps Going Out
art: The eleven signs are told by the Prophet ﷺ in the hadith of al-Bukhari 7121 (Sahih Muslim 2935): among them, religious knowledge is taken away and time passes quickly. This scene draws on that hadith, not on the Quran.
Nothing of anyone's belief is shown: the small lights are the lamps of a town, and a town going dark is the sign's picture.
The town and the lights are imagined.
The look of the town is imagined; its mud-brick walls and flat roofs are of the kind built in this people's time.
imagePrompt: A low town of pale stone at dusk, its streets and windows filled with countless small warm lamps; then, one street at a time, the lamps going out, until only a few are left burning and the town stands in a blue dusk; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: Before the Hour comes, the signs appear one by one, and the Prophet ﷺ told of them: that religious knowledge would be taken away, that earthquakes would increase, and that time would pass quickly.
The lamps of a town go out from one end to the other. Nobody blows them out. There is simply less and less light, until what is left is barely enough to walk by.

verse.en: A soul will [then] know what it has brought [with it].
